Reports from the interior confirm that Mzilikazi's Ndebele kingdom has established a new centre north of its former Transvaal lands. Defeat and displacement on the southern frontier have been followed by a difficult movement of households, herds and fighting men. Behind them, the emigrant settlement at Potchefstroom is consolidating its position. Ahead lies country with its own communities and political claims, where the newcomers must build their authority through fresh struggles and arrangements. The retreat has changed the balance of power across the region, rather than brought its conflicts to an end. Traders, neighbouring rulers and colonial officials are now adjusting their calculations to a Boer foothold in the south and a re-established Ndebele state in the north.
The interior enters a new chapter.

Mzilikazi's Ndebele kingdom has re-established itself north of its former Transvaal territory following defeat and displacement in the south. The migration has carried households, herds and military followers into a new political landscape, while the emigrants at Potchefstroom consolidate their position. Neighbouring communities and traders now face a changed balance of power across the interior.

Reports confirm the Ndebele migration north and the re-establishment of Mzilikazi's kingdom beyond its former Transvaal territory. Potchefstroom's settlers have gained ground in the south, changing the regional balance of power.
Mzilikazi's kingdom has moved north, while Potchefstroom consolidates its position in the Transvaal.
